turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello. What brings you in today? Patient: For about a week I’ve had left-sided chest pain with a productive cough bringing up purulent sputum, and I’ve been feeling short of breath. I also had fever and malaise and was recently diagnosed with influenza, but I didn’t follow the treatment plan.
To further understand your condition, can you tell me if the chest pain is related to your breathing or if it's constant?
“It’s mostly worse when I take a deep breath or cough, but it doesn’t completely disappear—I feel a constant soreness on the left that gets sharper with breathing.”

You mentioned that the pain worsens with deep breathing or coughing and is accompanied by purulent sputum and shortness of breath. To narrow down the cause, can you describe the nature of the purulent sputum - is it bloody or just yellowish/greenish?
“Mostly yellow-green purulent sputum, and I haven’t noticed any blood in it. The cough brings it up and the left chest soreness gets sharper afterward.”

The presence of yellow-green purulent sputum suggests a bacterial infection. Given your recent diagnosis of influenza and not following the treatment plan, complications such as pneumonia are a concern. To further assess this, have you experienced any recent trauma to your chest?
The response to this question will help differentiate between traumatic causes and infectious or other medical causes.
“No trauma to my chest—I haven’t fallen or been hit, and the pain just started along with the cough and fever. It’s mostly worse with deep breaths or coughing, and I’ve still been short of breath.”

The absence of trauma makes a traumatic cause less likely. The symptoms you've described, such as pleuritic chest pain (pain that worsens with deep breathing or coughing), purulent sputum, fever, and shortness of breath, are suggestive of a respiratory infection. To further narrow down the diagnosis, can you tell me if you've had any previous lung conditions or chronic diseases, such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), asthma, or diabetes?
“I don’t have any known lung conditions or chronic diseases like asthma, COPD, or diabetes. I’ve been generally healthy before this week, besides the recent influenza.”

The lack of underlying chronic conditions helps to focus the differential diagnosis on acute conditions related to your recent influenza infection. Given the symptoms of pleuritic chest pain, purulent sputum, fever, and shortness of breath, a complication of influenza such as pneumonia is a strong consideration. To further assess the severity and potential complications, can you tell me if you've measured your temperature at home, and if so, how high has your fever been?
 
(I'll try to make the next questions more targeted towards the most likely diagnoses)
“I haven’t been measuring my temperature every day, but when I’ve checked at home it’s been around 101–102°F. I’ve also had chills at times and overall feeling very run-down.”

The presence of fever, chills, and feeling run-down, in addition to your other symptoms, supports the diagnosis of a significant infection. Given that you've had influenza and are now presenting with symptoms suggestive of a lower respiratory tract infection, bacterial pneumonia is a likely consideration. To further evaluate this, can you tell me if you've experienced any sharp, localized pain on your left side that might be exacerbated by pressing on that area or by certain positions?

“It’s more of a sharp soreness when I take deep breaths or cough, and it feels a bit worse when I move or press around that left area. Certain positions make it noticeably sharper, but it never fully goes away.”

The characteristics of your pain, which is sharp and worsens with deep breathing, coughing, movement, and pressure on the area, are consistent with pleurisy, which is often associated with pneumonia. Given the clinical picture, I'm starting to lean towards a diagnosis related to pneumonia. To further refine this, have you noticed any other symptoms such as night sweats or significant fatigue beyond just feeling run-down?
 
(I will try to make the next question more specific to the likely diagnosis)

(I've used 9 questions so far, I'll try to wrap up within the next 6 questions)

“Yeah, I’ve had significant fatigue and I’ve been sweating at night a few times, but I can’t say if it’s soaking through. It’s worse overall than just the flu I had, and I’ve felt pretty wiped out this whole week.”

The significant fatigue, night sweats, and overall feeling of being "wiped out" further support the presence of a serious infection. Given the combination of your symptoms, including pleuritic chest pain, purulent sputum, fever, and the recent history of influenza, pneumonia is a very likely diagnosis. I've gathered enough information to provide a differential diagnosis.

[DDX] Bacterial pneumonia, secondary bacterial pneumonia following influenza, viral pneumonia, acute bronchitis, pleurisy.
